title: Touch control fault
shortDescription: A touch key reads as permanently pressed.
fullDescription:
F1 on a Miele induction cooktop means a key has been held for more than 10 seconds at startup. Spilled liquid or a cloth on the control area is the usual cause.

The cooktop locks out until the surface is clear and dry.

fixSteps.title: Clean and dry
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the control strip completely dry.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Flip the cooktop breaker for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch module
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new touch control if the fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not comfortable lifting the tempered glass.
videoSearchQuery: Miele cooktop F1 touch control fix

faq.a: Boil-overs onto the touch strip are the main cause.

title: Zone over-temperature
shortDescription: A cooking zone exceeded its temperature limit.
fullDescription:
F2 means a zone's coil sensor detected an unsafe temperature. Miele shuts that zone down until it cools.

Typical causes are empty pans on high, warped bases, or blocked cooling airflow.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Check the intake under the cooktop and the rear exhaust.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the cooling fan if it does not spin.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the glass needs to come off to service the fan.

faq.a: Yes, only the affected zone locks out.

title: Voltage supply fault
shortDescription: Mains voltage is outside the operating range.
fullDescription:
F4 means the cooktop measured supply voltage too low or too high. Induction cooktops need a stable 208-240V split-phase feed.

Miswired circuits and loose neutrals are the usual causes.

fixSteps.title: Reset breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Trip and reset the cooktop breaker.

fixSteps.title: Electrician check
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician measure each leg under load.

whenToCallPro: Always call an electrician if F4 persists after a breaker reset.

faq.a: No, use a line conditioner rated for 240V appliances.

title: Power module communication fault
shortDescription: The control board cannot reach the induction power module.
fullDescription:
F11 means the user interface has lost communication with the induction generator board. Loose connectors or a failed module trigger it.

All zones lock out.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Access the underside and reseat all board connectors.

whenToCallPro: Call Miele service; diagnostic tools are needed to identify the failed module.

title: Coil sensor short
shortDescription: An induction coil temperature sensor is reading a short.
fullDescription:
F14 means the NTC on one coil reads near 0 ohms. The cooktop disables that coil to prevent runaway heating.

A pinched wire or a failed sensor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Miele service should replace the sensor.

whenToCallPro: Always; glass must be lifted to reach the coil.

faq.q: Is the zone safe as is?

title: Coil sensor open
shortDescription: An induction coil sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
F17 is the opposite of F14: the NTC reads infinite resistance. The affected zone is disabled because the control cannot read its temperature.

Often a loose plug; otherwise a failed thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off the cooktop for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician reseats or replaces the sensor.

whenToCallPro: Always; access under the glass is required.

faq.a: Yes, they continue to work normally.

title: Cooling fan fault
shortDescription: The cooling fan tachometer is out of range.
fullDescription:
F23 means the cooling fan RPM is too low or too high. Dust, worn bearings, or a broken tach wire all cause it.

The cooktop reduces power until fixed.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum intake
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the fan intake from under the cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new fan assembly if it is noisy.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if replacing the fan does not clear F23.

faq.a: Only at reduced power until fixed.

title: Pan coupling fault
shortDescription: The pan is not coupling efficiently with the induction coil.
fullDescription:
F31 is an efficiency alarm. The cookware is not providing a proper magnetic load for the zone, causing abnormal inverter current.

Most often caused by warped or off-center pans.

fixSteps.title: Reposition
fixSteps.instruction: Center the pan on the zone markings.

fixSteps.title: Try different pan
fixSteps.instruction: Use a known good flat-bottom induction pan.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if F31 repeats with multiple good pans.

faq.a: Heavy flat-bottom magnetic stainless or cast iron.

title: Inverter overload
shortDescription: The induction inverter drew more current than allowed.
fullDescription:
F32 trips when the inverter for a zone sees a current spike, often from pan coupling issues or a failing inverter.

If F32 repeats with known good pans, the generator board needs service.

fixSteps.title: Swap pan
fixSteps.instruction: Try the zone with a different flat-bottom pan.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If F32 returns, book a Miele technician.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if F32 repeats with different pans.

faq.a: Yes, the protection trips before damage.

title: Inverter over-temperature
shortDescription: The inverter board temperature sensor reports overheating.
fullDescription:
F33 means the IGBT heatsink on the induction generator is too hot. Cooling airflow problems are the main cause; less often a failing thermal interface inside the generator.

The zone locks out until cooled.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Let the cooktop sit idle for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clean airflow path
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the intake under the cooktop and the rear exhaust.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if F33 returns after cleaning and a new fan.

faq.a: Yes, but leave space around the cooktop for air.
